We need propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to construct JSON with reactions and molecules.

We have target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Structure: a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (cinnamamide) with an aniline at the amide nitrogen (anilide). So overall: p-methyl phenyl-sulfonyl-para-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide is attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 para? Wait: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an extra NH2? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline with an amino at position 1 and another at position? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N means an aniline with an amino at both positions? That's a diamino benzene (phenylenediamine). So the amide nitrogen attached to a phenyl ring that also has an NH2 substituent (para? unspecified). So product is a sulfonamide linking two phenyl rings, one with tolyl, the other with a cinnamamide attached to a diamino phenyl.

We need retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide bond to get sulfonyl chloride + aniline? Or break amide bond to get acid + aniline? Also break the C=C double bond maybe via Heck? Simpler: disconnection at sulfonamide: use sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) and aniline (the phenyl-sulfonamide part). The sulfonyl chloride could be 4-methylphenylsulfonyl chloride (p-tolylsulfonyl chloride). That's commercially available? Likely yes. Check price? Not yet.

Second disconnection: amide bond between cinnamic acid derivative and aniline (phenylenediamine). Could use cinnamic acid (or its activated form) and aniline (phenylenediamine). The cinnamic acid part includes the trans double bond and carbonyl. So we can use trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-4-...?). Actually the phenyl attached to sulfonyl is the same phenyl that bears the cinnamoyl group. So we need to attach the cinnamoyl group to that phenyl via a carbonyl (amide). So we can start from 4-(cinnamoyl)aniline? Wait the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl is c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So it's a phenyl with a para-substituted cinnamoyl anilide? The substituent is at position? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 meaning the phenyl has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the phenyl is attached to sulfonyl at one position, and the side chain at para? Not important.

Thus retrosynthesis: Step 1: sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the phenyl with side chain) -> sulfonamide.

Step 2: The aniline (phenyl with side chain) could be formed by amide coupling of 4-aminophenyl (with NH2) and trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or acid). Actually we need the phenyl bearing both the sulfonyl attachment (via N) and the side chain (cinnamoyl). The phenyl is attached to sulfonyl via N (sulfonamide). So the phenyl is the nucleophile (aniline) that reacts with sulfonyl chloride. That phenyl also has a side chain amide attached to its para position (or meta). So we need to have that phenyl already functionalized with the amide side chain before sulfonylation. So we can first form the amide: start from 4-aminophenyl (with NH2) and trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or acid) to give 4-(cinnamoylamido)aniline (i.e., aniline with amide). Then sulfonylate the other amine (the one attached to sulfonyl) using p-tolylsulfonyl chloride.

Thus route: Step A (retrosynthesis): target -> disconnection of sulfonamide -> precursors: p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (ClSO2C6H4CH3) and 4-(cinnamoylamido)aniline (the phenyl with amide). Step B: disconnection of amide -> precursors: trans-cinnamic acid (or trans-cinnamoyl chloride) and 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine). Actually we need aniline with two amino groups: one will become sulfonamide, the other will become amide. So starting material could be p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). That's commercially available. Then we can acylate one amino group with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give 4-(cinnamoylamido)aniline. Then sulfonylate the other amino with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride.

Thus three steps total: 1) Acylation (amide formation) of p-phenylenediamine with trans-cinnamoyl chloride (or acid + coupling reagent). 2) Sulfonylation with p-tolylsulfonyl chloride. That's only two steps. But we also need to maybe protect the other amine during acylation to avoid double acylation. Could use protecting group like Boc, then deprotect later. But we can rely on selective acylation due to different reactivity? p-phenylenediamine both amines similar; may need protection. Could use mono-protection with Boc, then acylate, then deprotect, then sulfonylate. That would be 3 steps.

Alternatively, we could start from p-toluidine (para-methyl aniline) and sulfonylate with sulfonyl chloride derived from 4-aminophenyl? Not.

Better route: Use p-tolylsulfonyl chloride (commercial) and 4-(cinnamoylamido)aniline (commercial?). Check if 4-(cinnamoylamido)aniline is available. Search.
